A Michelin Star That Is Simply Not Deserved. Very Disappointing
Oct 2026 • Couples
We visited this Michelin-starred restaurant in Saigon with high expectations and chose the 8-course tasting menu. Unfortunately, the entire experience was a major disappointment.

Not a single course impressed us with its flavours. The dishes lacked creativity, depth, and the exceptional taste you would expect from a Michelin-starred restaurant.

Even more disappointing was the pace of the evening. All eight courses were served, and the entire experience was over in just 90 minutes. It felt more like an industrial production line than a fine-dining experience. Everything seemed rushed, mechanical, and completely lacking in passion, emotion, or personal attention.

The service was equally disappointing. The staff spoke very limited English, making it difficult for them to explain the dishes properly or create the connection and atmosphere expected at this level.

Fine dining should be about exceptional flavours, hospitality, storytelling, and a memorable experience. Sadly, we experienced none of these.

For the price charged, this restaurant offers extremely poor value for money. In our opinion, it does not deserve its Michelin star.

We have enjoyed many fine-dining experiences around the world, but this was certainly one of the most disappointing. A Michelin star should represent excellence, not simply an expensive, rushed dinner.

Would we return? Absolutely not.

Elegance Without a Strong Sense of Identity
Aug 2026 • Solo
Royal Pavlion Lunch Set Menu B

Shark’s Fin Dumpling Served in Supreme Broth — The broth tasted clean and refined. However, the dumpling wrapper wasn’t as delicate as I expected and easily broke apart when picked up. The filling had a subtler flavor than most dumplings, which allowed the texture of the shark’s fin to stand out while also absorbing the broth. Overall, though, I wasn’t completely satisfied with this dish. Maybe it was because this was the first course and I also felt that the different components weren’t cohesive.

Three-Item Dim Sum — All three dim sum items were savory and had their own distinct personalities. I liked their crispiness and how none of them felt greasy. They were definitely well-executed and refined versions of familiar dim sum.

I would have appreciated it if the fried rice had been served before or alongside the Sautéed Beef and Steamed Garoupa Fillet. Instead, it arrived after I had already finished the beef and was halfway through the fish. I think having the fried rice earlier would have made the main courses feel more complete and allowed me to enjoy the dishes together as intended.

Sautéed Beef with Black Pepper Sauce — This dish was flavorful and savory, and the beef was tender. I was hoping for a little more smokiness, but the caramelization on the beef was well done and added plenty of flavor.

Steamed Garoupa Fillet with Bean Curd and Homemade Soya Sauce — The fish was perfectly cooked, with a delicate and moist texture. The homemade soya sauce was refined and not overly salty.

Double-Boiled Red Date with Lotus Seed and Ginkgo + Mango Cake Roll — The red date dessert was sweet, while the double-boiling produced a cleaner and more concentrated flavor without straying too far from the character of a classic Cantonese dessert. The mango cake roll was also delicious, and I would have loved to have more of it.

Honestly, after dining here, I’m still not entirely sure what Long Triều is trying to present itself as. The restaurant lacked a distinct personality for me. From the moment I entered, the atmosphere felt stiff and formal, and that feeling carried throughout the experience. The food itself was certainly not bad, but I would have appreciated the restaurant more if I had been able to identify a defining characteristic or unique point of view that sets Long Triều apart from other Cantonese fine-dining restaurants. Everything felt refined and polished, but I left without a strong sense of what makes Long Triều distinctly Long Triều. 

I went to Hong Kong a week after this to try more Cantonese dishes, and I don’t think my experience in this restaurant was memorable enough.

Style Over Substance, Long Trieu Doesn't Deserve Its Star
Jan 2026 • Family
Long Trieu presents an elegant facade with its stylish location and ornate décor, though the lavish design borders on ostentatious. Unfortunately, the aesthetic appeal is where the experience peaks. The service fell short of expectations throughout our meal. Staff made no effort to explain the dishes or guide us through the menu. More problematically, used plates were never replaced between courses; we dined from the same dinnerware from start to finish, a fundamental oversight in fine dining protocol.

The cuisine simply didn't measure up to a Michelin standard. The vegetarian menu was particularly disappointing, lacking any distinctive flavor or depth. The signature duck arrived dry and uninspired. Each dish felt pedestrian and uninspired, failing to justify the acclaim. While Long Trieu certainly invests in ambiance and presentation, it struggles to deliver where it truly matters, in the kitchen and at the table. The one-star Michelin rating feels undeserved. For the price point and acclaim, diners should expect far more attentive service and substantially better food. There are numerous restaurants offering superior quality without the pretension.

Expensive, no ambience
Dec 2025 • Couples
After finding this restaurant through a search of Michelin, and having eaten in some really lovely restaurants in Ho Chi Minh, we feel completely ripped off. We don’t mind paying for good food, but honestly, $350/head Australian was absolutely freaking ridiculous for the short and unpleasant experience!! Food was beautifully presented and the staff sweet, but everything was rushed, English very poor, the set menu (Thousand of Shining Stars) completely unbalanced (way too much soup) and lacking in flavour. Apart from the food, we felt like we were eating inside a mausoleum with no ambience at all. No music. No humour. No warmth. Just awkward, dead kind of silence apart from the thrum of some kind of disco or sales conference music booming down the floor above. We kind of wished we were up there with them. Especially when we got slugged with a bill with all kinds of extra taxes - a 5% service charge plus 18% in extra VAT. For 2 of us our meal cost 11,858,752. Our bottle of wine, a lovely French Pinot, was 2,388,000 but honestly, if you’re looking for a great meal in Saigon, this place is just horribly overpriced for what you get. An awkward and expensive experience.
